title: Geometric irreducibility and purely transcendental extensions
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Geometric irreducibility of an extension $L/F$ means geometric irreducibility of the $F$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. If $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible, then for every finite algebraically independent family $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ over $K$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree], the extension $K(t_1,\ldots,t_r)/k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ is geometrically irreducible. Here adjoining the variables means forming successive rational function fields [def-weil-rational-function-field], and $r=0$ is allowed. Conversely, if $K(t)/k(t)$ is geometrically irreducible for one indeterminate $t$ over $K$, then $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible.

proof.text: For a field extension L/F, use the affine pullback isomorphism to identify each field base change of Spec L with Spec(L tensor_F E). Geometric irreducibility is therefore equivalent to irreducibility of every such tensor spectrum. We use the nilradical criterion for irreducibility. An injective ring map reflects nilpotence, so the source nilradical is the inverse image of the target nilradical; its primality, and thus irreducibility, descends. For a localization A -> B with B nonzero, localization commutes with radicals. If the nilradical of A is prime, it is disjoint from the denominator set: otherwise a unit in the nonzero ring B would be nilpotent. Its localized ideal is the prime nilradical of B. This proves the localization step without assuming reducedness.

source.place: Tag 0G31, forward localization argument; Tag 00ES, nilradical criterion; Mathlib IsLocalization.map_radical and isPrime_of_isPrime_disjoint

proof.text: Extend the tensor criterion from test fields in the universe of k to arbitrary larger test fields E. Put Omega = AlgebraicClosure k. The original hypothesis makes Spec(Omega tensor_k K) irreducible. Embed Omega and E over k into a common field M. Over the separably closed field Omega, the tensor-irreducibility theorem makes Spec(M tensor_Omega (Omega tensor_k K)) irreducible. Tensor reassociation identifies this with Spec(M tensor_k K). Flatness of vector spaces preserves the injection E -> M after tensoring with K; the injection argument of step 1 descends irreducibility to Spec(E tensor_k K). Commuting the factors gives the form used below.

source.place: Tag 0G31, the arbitrary field test in the forward argument; Tag 00I7; universe enlargement via common extensions

proof.text: For the given family t, put P = k[T_1,...,T_r], Q = K[T_1,...,T_r], F = k(t_1,...,t_r), and L = K(t_1,...,t_r). Algebraic independence over K restricts to k. The canonical evaluation equivalences from FractionRing(P) to F and FractionRing(Q) to L give actual fraction-field structures, and their polynomial maps commute with the displayed inclusion F -> L: check constants and variables after embedding both fields into the ambient field. Polynomial scalar extension is a pushout k -> K, P -> Q. Thus, for every E/F, tensor pushout cancellation identifies Q tensor_P E with K tensor_k E, whose spectrum is irreducible by step 2.

source.place: Tag 0G31, polynomial and fraction-field calculation, performed for all finite variables at once; Mathlib AlgebraicIndependent.aevalEquivField and MvPolynomial polynomial pushout

proof.text: Base change of the localization Q -> L shows that L tensor_P E is a localization of Q tensor_P E. Since F is a localization of P and both L and E are F-algebras, tensoring them over P or over F gives canonically isomorphic rings. The latter tensor product is nonzero by nontriviality of a tensor product of nonzero vector spaces over a field. Step 1 therefore gives irreducibility of Spec(L tensor_F E). The tensor criterion proves L/F geometrically irreducible. This argument includes the empty family and does not require induction or any additional transcendence assertion.

source.place: Tag 0G31, forward localization after scalar extension; Mathlib IsLocalization.algebraTensorEquiv

proof.text: For descent, a nonconstant rational function over k is transcendental over k (Mathlib RatFunc.transcendental_of_ne_C). Hence every element of k(t) algebraic over k is constant. The algebraically-closed-subfield criterion gives geometric irreducibility of k(t)/k. Compose this with the assumed geometric irreducibility of K(t)/k(t) to obtain geometric irreducibility of K(t)/k. The coefficient map used in the statement is exactly a k-algebra homomorphism by RatFunc.mapAlgHom, which supplies the scalar tower. For each E/k the injection K -> K(t) remains injective on tensoring with E. Step 1 descends irreducibility from Spec(K(t) tensor_k E) to Spec(K tensor_k E). The tensor criterion concludes geometric irreducibility of K/k.
